short: Not the best tank of the war, but the one built and shipped in tens of thousands.
full:
The pilot M4 was assembled at Lima Locomotive Works in February 1942, and the type first fought with the British Eighth Army at El Alamein that October, from a batch rushed to Egypt after the fall of Tobruk. Nearly 50,000 were produced. The design was shaped by logistics as much as tactics: it had to fit rail loading gauges, ships' derricks and military bridging, and it had to be repairable by conscript mechanics. It was reliable, and it arrived everywhere the Allies fought.

Against the Panther and Tiger from 1943 it was outgunned, and its early tendency to burn brought the nickname Ronson. The answers were incremental: a 76 mm gun, wet ammunition stowage that sharply cut fires, and the British Firefly conversion carrying a 17-pounder capable of killing any German tank it met. Shermans fought again in Korea, and the last American gun tank version was declared obsolete in March 1957. Israeli rebuilds with French guns were still in service into the 1980s.
